organization: World Meteorological Organization — State of the Climate in Asia 2024
region: Nationwide (China); Yellow and East China seas
notes: WMO press release on the State of the Climate in Asia 2024 report states: monthly average temperature records were broken in China in April, May, August, September and November 2024; drought in China affected nearly 4.8 million people, damaged 335,200 hectares of crops and caused an estimated 2.89 billion CNY (>USD 400 million) in direct losses; Tropical Cyclone Yagi, the strongest storm of the year in the region, caused widespread damage and casualties in China among other countries; sea-level rise on the Pacific side of Asia exceeded the global average; the Yellow and East China seas were especially affected by marine heatwaves.
recommended_action: Use WMO-verified 2024 loss figures as anchor evidence in HydraShield's China country risk profile; pitch multi-hazard monitoring and historical_event_intelligence to Chinese exposure holders referencing documented drought, heat and typhoon losses.
